title: Three moving targets land where their catalogues say
claim: From the image the WISE telescope took in 2010 to SPHEREx's latest visit, Epsilon Indi B, Barnard's Star and WISE 0855-0714 moved across the sky by the amount their catalogue astrometry gives.
test: The 2010 position is the centre of a Gaussian fitted in the AllWISE Atlas image of band W2 (for a star that saturates WISE, the centroid of the wings of its image); the SPHEREx position is the mean over the photos of the latest deep visit of detector 6 (the two stars) or the centre in the co-add of that visit (WISE 0855, too faint for one photo; a Gaia star beside it is fitted with it). The catalogue position is Gaia DR3 for the two stars and the astrometry of Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 as served by SIMBAD for WISE 0855 (not in Gaia; the paper itself was not opened), moved to each date with proper motion and parallax. Position only: no brightness is produced for Barnard's Star or WISE 0855. Beside WISE 0855-0714 lies the star Gaia DR3 5756956644387831296 (G 16.3), 4.3 arcsec from it at the date of the SPHEREx visit; it does not move and is fitted together with the target. In the 2010 image the target was 131 arcsec away, and what that image shows at the star's place lies 0.23 arcsec (0.04 of a SPHEREx pixel) from the star's Gaia position at that date (rule of the review: within 1 pixel).
pass_rule: Each measured shift differs from the catalogue shift by at most the tolerance in site/data/targets/tolerances.json (written before the jobs measured: half a SPHEREx pixel, plus half of what the object moved while the 2010 image was taken, plus one WISE beam for a star that saturates WISE), and each SPHEREx position lies within half a pixel of the catalogue position at that date. A fixed star beside a target is seen in the 2010 image within one SPHEREx pixel of its Gaia position. Barnard's Star saturates WISE: the core of its 2010 image is spoiled, and a Gaussian fitted there lands 6.4 arcsec from the catalogue, on the brighter side of the core. That value is not used. Its 2010 centre is the centroid of the wings of its image (2 to 4 beam widths out, started from the fit and repeated until it settles), 0.3 arcsec from the catalogue. The WISE beam in its tolerance (6.4 arcsec) was set when only the first value was known; without it the tolerance would be 5.8 arcsec and the difference of 0.1 arcsec would be within it all the same.
value: Epsilon Indi B 0.5 arcsec (0.14 px in SPHEREx alone); Barnard's Star 0.1 arcsec (0.04 px in SPHEREx alone); WISE 0855-0714 0.7 arcsec (0.07 px in SPHEREx alone)
unit: difference between measured and catalogue shift
reference: Epsilon Indi B 73.9 arcsec in 15.8 years; Barnard's Star 163.8 arcsec in 15.8 years; WISE 0855-0714 128.6 arcsec in 15.7 years
tolerance: Epsilon Indi B 4.2 arcsec; Barnard's Star 12.2 arcsec; WISE 0855-0714 4.8 arcsec; 0.5 px in SPHEREx alone

title: Motion within SPHEREx's own year
claim: Between two SPHEREx visits months apart, Epsilon Indi B and WISE 0855-0714 are seen to move, by the amount their catalogue astrometry gives with parallax included.
test: Detector 6. Epsilon Indi B: its position in every photo, averaged over each visit; first against last deep visit. WISE 0855: its position in the co-add of each of two visits (at each pixel the mean of the photos that may be used there; a Gaia star beside it is fitted with it); May 2025 is left out. It is measured a second time from only the photos with no unusable pixel round the target. Field stars measured the same way in the same photos are the control; the scatter of their shifts is added to the target's error.
pass_rule: Per target: the measured shift is at least 3 times its error from zero, and its east and north components are each within 3 times their error of the catalogue shift. The rule is applied with the robust scatter of the field stars in the error (the value given) and again with their plain standard deviation, and for WISE 0855 with both choices of photos; a target is shown only if it holds every way. A target that does not meet the rule gets its measured shift and error stated, and no motion view.
plain: motion seen within SPHEREx's own year
value: Epsilon Indi B 4.78 +- 0.15 arcsec; WISE 0855-0714 3.15 +- 0.83 arcsec
reference: Epsilon Indi B 4.66 arcsec; WISE 0855-0714 4.57 arcsec

title: RW Aurigae: its change per colour, with the saturated centre left out
claim: Between September 2025 and February to March 2026 RW Aurigae changed by a different amount in each colour band; a band is shown only where the change does not rest on pixels close to saturation.
test: Per detector, every one-to-one pair of frames the match rule accepts between the two visits. Three ways: all pairs (aperture of 3 pixels, every pixel); a common mask (in both frames everything within the radius that holds every flagged pixel of either aperture is left out, and the flux is that of the ring from there to 4.5 pixels); clean pairs (no flagged pixel in either aperture). Twenty comparison stars in the same frames are measured the same way, with the mask radius of the RW Aurigae pair nearest in colour. No data of other observers are used.
pass_rule: Per band: the sign of the change is the same with the common mask as with all pairs, and the comparison stars of that band, with the same mask, have a median ratio within 1% of 1. A band that fails reads "too bright to measure reliably".
value: D1 +18.8% (13 pairs) not shown; D2 +36.0% (11 pairs); D3 +28.2% (14 pairs); D4 not measurable; D5 -28.1% (7 pairs) not shown; D6 -37.6% (8 pairs) not shown
unit: change with the common mask, per detector

title: R Draconis is too bright to measure
claim: R Draconis is saturated in every SPHEREx photo of this release that holds it, so the tool gives no brightness for it.
test: Every photo that holds the star, in all six detectors, from 2025-05-16 to 2026-05-13: the flags of the pixels within 3 pixels of the star's position.
pass_rule: A photo is saturated when at least one of those pixels carries the flag OVERFLOW, NONLINEAR or BLOOM. The verdict "too bright to measure" stands if every photo checked is saturated.

title: A plain blink makes steady stars seem to change
claim: Flipping through SPHEREx photos that were taken at different colours makes steady stars seem to change in brightness; between photos of the same colour they hold.
test: Twenty steady comparison stars in the frames of RW Aurigae. The swing of a star is its brightest flux over its faintest (aperture of 3 pixels) among the photos flipped through: every photo of the first visit in time order (112 photos, six detectors); the photos of detector 1 in that visit; the two photos of a pair matched at the same colour in detector 1 (median over the star's pairs). The value is the median over the stars; RW Aurigae's own swing is given beside it.
pass_rule: The median swing of the comparison stars between matched photos is below 1.10, and below their swing at the other two stops.
plain: steady stars hold once the colour is matched
unit: median swing of the comparison stars
reference: RW Aurigae itself: x 49.7, x 2.71, x 1.24
